title: Iran–US Ceasefire Declared; Hormuz Normalization to Ease Saudi Oil Export Crisis
detail: A ceasefire between the United States and Iran was declared on May 29, 2026, ending the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports that had been in effect since April 13. The agreement included Iranian commitments to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — which had been closed to commercial shipping since February 28 — as part of broader nuclear talks. For Saudi Arabia, the ceasefire represents the most significant economic relief since the Hormuz crisis began: the Kingdom's oil production has been suppressed to approximately 6.77 million bpd versus its quota of 10.291 million bpd, costing an estimated SAR 125.7B ($33.5B) in Q1 2026 alone. Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province oil fields had been forced to operate at roughly two-thirds of capacity with no viable eastern export route. The White House Deputy Chief of Staff indicated Iran had made significant concessions including agreement in principle to Hormuz normalization. Saudi officials did not comment publicly but were reported to have received private briefings from Washington ahead of the announcement.

media.caption: Iran–US ceasefire ends blockade; Strait of Hormuz normalization expected to ease Saudi oil export crisis

title: Houthi Leader Declares Iran Ceasefire a 'Great Victory,' Warns of Further Attacks on Red Sea
detail: Houthi Supreme Leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi declared the Iran–US ceasefire a 'great victory for the Axis of Resistance' on May 29, while simultaneously warning that the Houthi movement reserves the right to resume attacks 'depending on future developments.' The declaration raised immediate alarm in Riyadh: if the Houthis remain independently hostile to Saudi Red Sea shipping after the US-Iran ceasefire, Saudi Arabia's strategic pivot to the Red Sea corridor — which Chatham House identified in a May 27 analysis as the primary alternative to the Hormuz route — faces a new chokepoint threat at Bab el-Mandeb. Saudi Arabia's MARAD-flagged Red Sea corridor depends on Bab el-Mandeb passage. The Houthi declaration underscored the structural risk in Saudi Arabia's logistics reorientation: escaping Hormuz dependency may mean deeper exposure to Houthi interdiction in the Red Sea — a threat Saudi Arabia cannot easily suppress without a full resumption of the Yemen war it has been trying to end.

media.caption: Houthi leader declares Iran ceasefire 'great victory,' warns of further attacks on Red Sea shipping
